Subject: Question on DSR -> invoices / monthly statements

Hi Markus,

Quick question from procurement here at Sumo Analytics — we have a customer-initiated data subject request that asks for deletion of user-level data and associated PII. Before we proceed on our side, our auditors asked us to confirm whether Redwood will retain any accounting artefacts that could be tied back to deleted users: specifically monthly statements, invoice PDFs, and the raw per-request usage logs that feed billing reports.

Two related asks:
- Can you confirm whether monthly invoices and the billing ledger are retained after a DSR and, if so, for how long?
- Are billing exports/usage logs stored in an identifiable form (with user identifiers) or only as aggregated/hashed records? Also: does residency (EU vs US) affect what you keep?

We may need a short written confirmation for our auditors. Appreciate a quick pointer or a template statement we can include in our compliance pack.

Thanks,
Elena Rossi

Elena — thanks for the clear questions. Short answer up front: invoices and the accounting ledger are retained for statutory and audit purposes even if a DSR for user content is fulfilled; however we can provide redacted copies and auditor-friendly extracts that do not include customer PII. Residency influences how we store customer-data-bearing artifacts (EU customers can be stored exclusively in EU regions when contracted).

High-level points:
- Invoices and the billing ledger are considered financial records. Redwood retains them for 7 years for accounting and tax compliance (standard practice for the jurisdictions we operate in).
- Usage logs used for billing are processed into aggregated billing records. Per-request logs that contain user identifiers are not retained longer than necessary for troubleshooting (default 90 days), unless preserved under legal hold or contract.
- When a valid DSR requests erasure of personal data, we:
  1) delete personal identifiers from product logs and customer-managed data stores per the DSR scope,
  2) preserve accounting records (invoices/ledger) as required by law, but provide redacted versions that remove or pseudonymize PII for your auditors if needed.
- For customers with EU residency requirements (and those on a Private deployment), invoices and any customer-attributable billing exports can be kept in-region. Hosted customers can opt into EU-only storage via contract addenda.

I'm attaching a quick redacted sample invoice to show the level of redaction we can do. If you need a formal attestation for your auditors, I'll loop in Neha and Marissa to provide a written statement and an export procedure.

Best,
Markus Klein
Director, Finance — Redwood Inference

Hi Elena and team,

Following Markus' note, please find a formal summary of our position for inclusion in your audit pack. I've kept this concise — happy to expand if your auditors need more detail.

Redwood Inference — Data Retention & Billing Records (summary for auditors):
- Accounting Records: Invoice PDFs, billing ledger entries, and journal entries are retained for a mandatory retention period of 7 years to satisfy tax and financial reporting requirements across our operating jurisdictions. These records are classified as financial records and are excluded from routine erasure under DSRs to the extent required by law.
- Usage Data & Logs: Raw per-request logs that include customer-supplied identifiers are retained for troubleshooting and internal analytics for up to 90 days by default. Prior to reaching the 90-day window, logs are aggregated and/or pseudonymized so that long-term billing computations no longer contain direct personal identifiers.
- Redaction & Auditor Exports: Upon request we can produce redacted invoice PDFs and reconciliations that include line-item usage while removing personal identifiers (API keys, end-user email addresses, IPs). For auditors requiring reconciliation granularity, we offer:
  * Aggregated line items (endpoint + product SKU + total usage) for historic periods, or
  * Pseudonymized mappings (non-reversible IDs) to allow reconciliation without exposing PII.
- Residency Controls: For customers with region-specific contracts, billing records and invoice storage can be limited to the contracted region (e.g., EU-only storage). Please confirm your residency clause in the customer contract if you require strict in-region evidence.
- Legal Hold / Exceptions: If there is an active legal hold, preservation requirements override DSR-based erasure. We will notify customers if any legal preservation is in effect.

Next steps we recommend:
1) Confirm whether Sumo needs full line-item exports (aggregated or pseudonymized) or only redacted PDFs.
2) If in-region storage is required, confirm the residency clause so we can validate the storage location for the requested records.
3) We will produce a signed data preservation statement (attached) and provide step-by-step instructions for generating auditor-friendly exports.

I've attached a short statement for your auditors and a one-page export guide. If your auditors need an attestation on company letterhead, let me know and we'll get that signed via DocuSign (link included below).

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Privacy & Compliance — Redwood Inference

Hi Elena — copying practical next steps from Finance so your team can plan timelines: 

- Historic invoices (FY2026): We can produce redacted PDFs for the full FY2026 period within 5 business days after you confirm scope. Redaction will remove direct identifiers (email, API keys, IP addresses) while keeping invoice line items and totals intact.
- Auditor exports (CSV): If you need a reconciliation CSV with aggregated usage buckets, expect a 7-10 business day turnaround; we will provide either aggregated endpoint-level lines or pseudonymized mapping depending on your preference.
- Residency checks: Please confirm whether Sumo is on an EU-residency contract. If yes, we'll validate the region where the historic exports are served from and include that confirmation in our attestation.
- Cost: There is no charge for one compliance export per audit cycle for active customers; additional ad-hoc requests may be billable (we'll flag this in the delivery email if applicable).

Action items for you: reply to this thread with (A) which output you prefer (redacted PDFs vs CSV aggregated exports vs pseudonymized mapping) and (B) whether you have an EU-residency clause. We'll kick off the export and follow-up with a secure link for retrieval.
